title: A button you can press never looks disabled: the remove x on an effect reads as bright as the eye beside it
goal: Every icon button that works looks like it works. The x that removes an effect, the reorder grip beside it, and every other active icon button in the panels are drawn at the same strength as their working neighbours (like the eye). Faint grey is kept for things that really are disabled.
notes: User, 2026-10-24: 'the "remove" x button on effects seems disabled but it is not. buttons which are active should not look diminished. look at the eye visibility icon button next to it.' Screenshot: queue/audits/2026-10-24-user-effect-remove-looks-disabled.png (Shadow effect: grip, eye bright, x faint). Confirmed in code: Sources/Photonz/EffectsListRow.swift:220-232 removeButton sets .foregroundStyle(.tertiary) on an enabled button, and the grip at :200-204 is .tertiary at rest. The same pattern is likely elsewhere: there are 93 .foregroundStyle(.tertiary) uses in Sources/Photonz, most of them text, so sort buttons from labels. Candidates to check: MotionListInspector.swift:186, PropertyKeysInspector.swift:689, MotionStripView.swift:247 and TimelineTrackRows.swift:1627 (xmarks), plus the Motion header's play button in the same screenshot, which also looks dim. Keep the mock's quiet look: quiet means the same tone as the eye, not fainter.
acceptance: The effect row's remove x and reorder grip are drawn in the same tone as its eye button at rest, and a little brighter on hover, in light and dark. Picture before and after in the audit

One rule in the panel kit decides an icon button's tone: enabled at rest, hovered, pressed, disabled. Disabled is the only state drawn faint. Row icon buttons use it instead of setting their own colour

Sweep: every icon-only button in the panels, dock, timeline headers and Ask rows that is enabled but drawn faint (.tertiary or a low opacity) is listed in the audit with its file and line, and moved onto the rule, or kept faint with a written reason (for example it is a hint, not a button)
A check (unit test or a walk that measures pixel contrast) fails when an enabled icon button is drawn fainter than the disabled tone plus a margin, so this cannot come back
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: 2026-10-24 triage: every audit this week was photographed with the window behind another app, which draws controls in their background look (audit-pictures-show-the-window-the-way-a-person, p2). For a task about how bright a button reads that matters: take the before and after pictures with the probe in front (PHOTONZ_IGNORE_PERSON=1 by hand, or a walk with setup front: true while the Mac is free), or measure the tone from the view itself, and say which in the audit.

Reproduced: EffectsListRow drew the cross at .tertiary and the grip at .tertiary at rest beside a .primary eye; a before run of active-icon-buttons-look-live-walk on the old code shows it (queue/audits/2026-11-02-icon-tone-1-at-rest-before-after.png), and the legibility sheet measured the old cross at 1.87:1 light / 2.24:1 dark against a disabled icon's 1.83 / 2.25.

Adversarial review: a Photoshop/Figma user expects row icons that work to read at label strength and only hidden or unavailable things to recede; the risk is a noisier Layers list once every open padlock comes up from tertiary. Chose a separate off tone (secondary label, 0.55) for switches that are off over keeping them tertiary because tertiary is the disabled tone and the user asked that only disabled reads faint; the audit asks whether the padlock column is still calm.

Chose a soft 4pt rounded wash on hover over brightening alone because 0.85 to 1.0 ink is too small a step to see on a 9pt cross; the transform link keeps its plain style and reads the rule directly so the wash does not cover its two-row bracket.

Built: IconButtonTone + FaintIconScan (PhotonzCore, tested), PanelIconButtonStyle/.panelIconTone (app), legibility sheet check louderThanDisabled with a negative control (the old faint cross must still fail). 14 buttons moved onto the rule, 4 kept faint with a quiet-on-purpose reason. Walks green: active-icon-buttons-look-live, appearance-effects, panel-edge-column, panel-edge-narrow, transform-values-link, properties-pane, motion-strip-way-back, layers-combine, colour-onto-a-layer-row, motion-one-play-rule, motion-swings-a-layer, timeline-zooms-out-past-the-end, lists-pane-holds-still, measure-lands-in-the-list, a-ring-or-arc-arrives-spinning, key-a-title-s-scale, effects-say-their-reach. Scripts/test.sh green (exit 0, legibility included).

Rough items, none filed: the mock-vs-app grip/eye tone is settled by the user's report; the secondary-resting icon buttons outside the panel (history overlay, transport kit) are not faint by this task's measure and nobody has reported them, so they stay in this log rather than a task. Note for runners: during this task a mistyped 'git stash push' (zsh does not split $VAR) fell through to a 'git stash pop' that popped stash@{0} (qwen-image leftovers); it was put back with 'git stash store' on the same commit 3583be9 and its files removed from the tree, so the stash list is as it was.

Shipped 14770731: one tone rule for panel icon buttons (IconButtonTone in PhotonzCore, PanelIconButtonStyle in the app). The effect row's cross and grip now match the eye at rest and brighten with a soft wash on hover, light and dark; 14 buttons moved onto the rule, 4 kept faint with written reasons (search clear buttons, section help mark). Guarded by FaintIconScanTests (source scan of every app file) and a measured check in the legibility sheet (every pressable icon at least 1.5x a disabled one's contrast; the old cross read 1.87:1 vs disabled 1.83:1, now 14.7:1). Verified: Scripts/test.sh green, 17 walks green incl. new active-icon-buttons-look-live-walk at Next defaults; before/after pictures in queue/audits/2026-11-02-a-button-you-can-press-never-looks-disabled-the.json.
